name: How a Paper Is Cited
title: How a Paper Is Cited
answer: How a paper is cited covers the conventions and mechanics by which a research work is referenced in later literature, including bibliographic fields, in-text citation forms, and the role of citation indexes in tracing influence. It also concerns the distinction between citing a paper and citing a claim extracted from it, which matters for evidence mapping. The topic sits within citation mapping and discovery, where the goal is to show not just that a paper was cited, but how and in what context.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: How a paper is cited covers the conventions and mechanics by which a research work is referenced in later literature, including bibliographic fields, in-text citation forms, and the role of citation indexes in tracing influence. It also concerns the distinction between citing a paper and citing a claim extracted from it, which matters for evidence mapping. The topic sits within citation mapping and discovery, where the goal is to show not just that a paper was cited, but how and in what context.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Citation mapping runs on structured bibliographic records, persistent identifiers such as DOIs, and databases of papers and extracted claims. This site's library of 135 research papers and 10,767 extracted claims is one such resource, alongside catalogues of 91 AI books, 803 scientific models, 732 AI tools and 674 glossary terms. The infrastructure must resolve references to the original paper rather than to a secondary search layer.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by parsing reference lists, matching each citation to a unique paper, and disambiguating authors, venues and versions. Citation contexts are then extracted from the citing text to record whether a claim is supported, contradicted or merely mentioned. The resulting citation graph links papers through directed edges, and claim-level extraction adds a finer layer of evidence to the graph.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk in citation work centre on provenance and accuracy. A citation must point to the original paper, not to an aggregator or search result, and this site follows that rule by never linking to the Consensus search tool and always linking to the original paper. Risks include miscitation, citation stacking and incomplete metadata, so provenance records should show where each citation and extracted claim came from.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Citation mapping is moving toward automated extraction of citation intent and context, so that a reader can see whether a paper is cited as background, method, comparison or critique. Open citation graphs and claim-level indexes are likely to become more common, and provenance will remain a core requirement as these systems scale. The direction is toward finer-grained, machine-readable citation records that still resolve to the original work.
